gallery.title: File:S65-58504 (25928743955).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description: S65-58504 (4 Nov. 1965) --- Astronauts Charles Conrad Jr., (right) prime crew command pilot, and Richard F. Gordon Jr., prime crew pilot, for the Gemini-Titan XI (GT-11) Earth-orbital mission. Photo credit: NASA (2016/03/20).

gallery.title: File:S66-50735 (25628158600).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description: S66-50735 (12 Sept. 1966) --- The Gemini-11 spacecraft, carrying astronauts Charles Conrad Jr., command pilot, and Richard F. Gordon Jr., pilot, was successfully launched by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration from the Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 19 at 9:42 a.m. (EST), Sept. 12, 1966. The liftoff photograph is framed by the sides of the lowered erector. Photo credit: NASA (2016/03/20).

gallery.title: File:S66-44497 (25300018073).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description: S66-44497 (23 July 1966) --- Astronauts Charles Conrad Jr. (left) and Richard F. Gordon Jr. (right), prime crew for the Gemini-11 spaceflight, practice water egress procedures in the Gulf of Mexico. Static Article 5 was used(2016/03/20). in the training exercise. A MSC swimmer is in the water assisting in the training. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.title: File:Postflight discussion of S-13 experiment (S66-45615).jpg
gallery.description: Discussing the S-13, Ultraviolet Astronomical Camera Experiment, during the postflight experiments briefing at the Manned Spacecraft Center, Houston, Texas, are (left to right) astronauts Charles Conrad Jr., Gemini-11 command pilot; Richard F. Gordon Jr., Gemini-11 pilot; and Dr. Karl Henize, Dearborn Observatory, Northwestern University.

gallery.title: File:Conrad wearing a Glycine Airman.jpg
gallery.description: S66-50715 (12 Sept. 1966) --- Astronaut Charles Conrad Jr., command pilot of the Gemini-11 spaceflight, undergoes suiting up operations in the Launch Complex 16 suit trailer during the Gemini-11 prelaunch countdown. Later, astronauts Conrad and Richard F. Gordon Jr., pilot, entered a transport van which carried them to Pad 19 and their waiting spacecraft in preparation for their scheduled three-day mission in space. Suit technician James L. Garrepy assists. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - MISC - EXPERIMENT D-16 - KNEE TETHER - MSC (s66-00933).jpg
gallery.title: File:GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - MISC - EXPERIMENT D-16 - KNEE TETHER - MSC (s66-00933).jpg
gallery.description: S66-00933 (28 Jan. 1966) --- Gemini-11 Experiment D-16 Knee Tether, sponsored by the Department of Defense and the United States Air Force. The astronaut tightens and loosens bolts in a prescribed pattern during his extravehicular activity, once with his body held to the spacecraft by a nine-inch tether looped around his knee and through the handrail, and once without the tether. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.title: File:PRESS CONFERENCE - GEMINI-11- ASTRONAUTS - MSC (s66-45605).jpg
gallery.description: S66-45605 (26 Sept. 1966) --- Movie film of the Gemini-11 extravehicular activity and rendezvous with the Agena Target Docking Vehicle was shown at the Gemini-11 press conference in the MSC Building 1 auditorium. Astronauts Charles Conrad Jr. (left), command pilot, and Richard F. Gordon Jr., pilot, discussed the Gemini-11 EVA and rendezvous mission during the film. Picture on screen shows close-up of astronaut Gordon connecting the Agena Target Vehicle to the spacecraft with a tether line during his spacewalk. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: GORDON, RICHARD F , ASTRONAUT - GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - EXPERIMENTS BRIEFING - MSC (s66-45614).jpg
gallery.title: File:GORDON, RICHARD F , ASTRONAUT - GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - EXPERIMENTS BRIEFING - MSC (s66-45614).jpg
gallery.description: S66-45614 (23 Sept. 1966) --- Astronauts Charles Conrad Jr. (with pipe) and Richard F. Gordon Jr. (background) view negatives from their Gemini-11 mission. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.title: File:MCC During GT-11 (s66-52762).jpg
gallery.description: S66-52762 (15 Sept. 1966) --- Dr. Robert R. Gilruth (left) smokes a cigar in Houston's Mission Control Center to celebrate the successful splashdown of Gemini-11. Looking on are James C. Elms (center), MSC deputy director, and Charles W. Mathews, Gemini program manager. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: Nose of Gemini 11 spacecraft and Agena Target Vehicle as seen during EVA (s66-54656).jpg
gallery.title: File:Nose of Gemini 11 spacecraft and Agena Target Vehicle as seen during EVA (s66-54656).jpg
gallery.description: S66-54656 (13 Sept. 1966) --- Nose of Gemini-11 spacecraft and Agena Target Vehicle while docked as photographed by astronaut Richard F. Gordon Jr., pilot, during his stand-up extravehicular activity (EVA). Taken with a modified 70mm Hasselblad camera, using Eastman Kodak, Ektachrome, MS (S.O. 368) color film. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: GORDON, RICHARD F , ASTRONAUT - MISC - GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - CAPE (s66-50720).jpg
gallery.title: File:GORDON, RICHARD F , ASTRONAUT - MISC - GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - CAPE (s66-50720).jpg
gallery.description: S66-50720 (12 Sept. 1966) --- Preparations are made in the white room atop Pad 19 to close the hatches on the Gemini-11 spacecraft just after insertion during the Gemini-11 prelaunch countdown. On the left is astronaut Charles Conrad Jr., command pilot; and on the right is Richard F. Gordon Jr., pilot. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.title: File:GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - ON PAD - ATLAS-AGENA - CAPE (s66-50724).jpg
gallery.description: S66-50724 (12 Sept. 1966) --- An Agena Target Docking Vehicle atop its Atlas launch vehicle is ready for launch at Launch Complex 14 at Cape Kennedy, Florida. The Agena served as a rendezvous and docking vehicle for the Gemini-11 spacecraft. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.title: File:GT-11 - PAD (S66-50765).jpg
gallery.description: S66-50765 (12 Sept. 1966) --- The erector at Launch Complex 19 is lowered during the Gemini-11 prelaunch countdown. Awaiting the launch in the Gemini-11 spacecraft atop the Gemini Launch Vehicle-11 are astronauts Charles Conrad Jr., command pilot, and Richard F. Gordon Jr., pilot. Liftoff was at 9:42 a.m. (EST), Sept. 12, 1966. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: Astronaut M Scott Carpenter monitors Booster System Console in MCC (s66-51794).jpg
gallery.title: File:Astronaut M Scott Carpenter monitors Booster System Console in MCC (s66-51794).jpg
gallery.description: S66-51794 (12 Sept. 1966) --- Astronaut M. Scott Carpenter monitors the Booster Systems Console in the Manned Spacecraft Center (MSC) Mission Control Center during launch of the Gemini-11 spaceflight. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: Personnel discussing Gemini 11 space flight in Mission Control (s66-52157).jpg
gallery.title: File:Personnel discussing Gemini 11 space flight in Mission Control (s66-52157).jpg
gallery.description: S66-52157 (12 Sept. 1966) --- Discussing the Gemini-11 spaceflight in the Mission Control Center are: (left to right) Christopher C. Kraft Jr., (wearing glasses), Director of Flight Operations; Charles W. Mathews (holding phone), Manager, Gemini Program Office; Dr. Donald K. Slayton (center, checked coat), Director of Flight Crew Operations; astronaut William A. Anders, and astronaut John W. Young. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - PRELAUNCH COUNTDOWN - ASTRONAUTS GORDON AND CONRAD - CAPE (s66-50780).jpg
gallery.title: File:GEMINI-TITAN (GT)-11 - PRELAUNCH COUNTDOWN - ASTRONAUTS GORDON AND CONRAD - CAPE (s66-50780).jpg
gallery.description: S66-50780 (10 Sept. 1966) --- Astronauts Richard F. Gordon Jr. (in front), pilot, and Charles Conrad Jr., command pilot, walk up the ramp at Pad 19 during the Gemini-11 prelaunch countdown. Photo credit: NASA

gallery.filename: Gemini 11 prime crew prepare to enter Gemini 11 spacecraft (s66-57967).jpg
gallery.title: File:Gemini 11 prime crew prepare to enter Gemini 11 spacecraft (s66-57967).jpg
gallery.description: S66-57967 (10 Sept. 1966) --- Gemini-11 prime crew, astronauts Charles Conrad Jr. (right), command pilot, and Richard F. Gordon Jr. (left), pilot, prepare to enter the Gemini-11 spacecraft in the White Room atop Pad 19. Photo credit: NASA
